call_overview.title: About the call
call_overview.question: What does the call offer, and who can apply?

cards.title: What the call wants
cards.question: What is the principal thing the project must develop, and which problem or need must it address?
cards.answer: Improve existing industrial recycling processes so they can handle mixed battery inputs and recover more valuable materials.
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 96–98 · Scope
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 96–98 · Expected Outcome

cards.title: Project impact
cards.question: Which wider system outcomes and impacts must the project support?
cards.answer: Recover critical materials more efficiently, reduce reliance on imports and meet recovery and sustainability requirements under the European Batteries Regulation.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 96–98 · Expected Outcome

cards.title: Who it suits
cards.question: Who may lead, which partners must take part, and how must the work be shared?
cards.answer: This suits battery recyclers, separation and process-equipment firms, and research organisations with access to an operating recycling process. The group needs three independent grant recipients in different eligible countries, including one in a European Union Member State. An eligible recipient coordinates. Control by China or by an entity based there prevents participation.

cards.title: Innovation
cards.question: How new must the project be, and in what must it innovate?
cards.answer: Demonstrate technical innovations in processing mixed battery materials. The call specifically targets improvements to scaled recycling technologies and processing of black mass (the powder from shredded cells).
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 96–98 · Scope

cards.title: Maturity
cards.question: Which maturity level is expected at the start and end of the project?
cards.answer: The work should reach TRL 6–7 (technology readiness level: technology demonstrated in relevant or operational conditions) by project end. The call allows work to start at any maturity level.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 96–98 · Specific conditions

cards.title: Demonstration and integration of work
cards.question: Where must the solution be demonstrated, and how must the work fit with existing systems?
cards.answer: Demonstrate recovery on variable input streams within an existing industrial process. Compare output quality, material recovery, costs and environmental performance.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 96–98 · Scope

call_overview.title: Relevance to TenneT
call_overview.question: Why is this call relevant to TenneT?

cards.title: Why it matters to TenneT
cards.question: Why does this call matter to TenneT, and why can't TenneT take part itself?
cards.answer: More dependable recovery of critical battery materials could lower supply risks for storage suppliers. The topic funds industrial recycling and sets out no transmission-operator work.

funding_timing_submission.title: Funding
funding_timing_submission.question: How much funding can the project receive?

cards.title: Funding envelope
cards.answer:
The Commission indicates EUR 18.8 million for industrial battery recycling. It expects 2 awards.
- Grant request: around EUR 9.4 million per project is indicative. The Commission can select a different request.
- Funding form: Budget-based grant (paid using approved costs or rates for the funded work).
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 96–98 · Specific conditions
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · p. 39 · Overview of this call
Improvement of Adaptability, Flexibility and Efficiency of Existing Recycling Processes (BATT4EU Partnership) · Budget overview

cards.title: Funding rate and co-financing
cards.answer:
For-profit organisations can receive up to 70% towards industrial battery recycling.
- For-profit organisations: Up to 70% of eligible costs (project costs the grant rules allow), leaving at least 30% to cover.
- Non-profit legal entities: Up to 100% of eligible costs (project costs the grant rules allow).

funding_timing_submission.title: Timing
funding_timing_submission.question: What timing should the proposal submission and project follow?

cards.title: Application route
cards.answer:
Apply for industrial battery recycling through the European Funding & Tenders Portal in one stage.
- Full proposal: 31 March 2027, 17:00 Brussels time. Submit Part A (online administration form) and Part B (technical proposal). Part B is limited to 40 pages.
- Opening: 3 December 2026.

cards.title: Project window
cards.answer:
The grant agreement (the contract setting the funded work and payment rules) sets the start date and duration for industrial battery recycling.
- Required start: Work normally starts after the grant agreement is signed. A reasoned exception needs approval.

cards.title: Evaluation and selection — scored or ranked
Conditional and exceptional requirements
cards.answer:
The battery recycling call has conditions on controlling interests and commercial use of results.
- Conditional — Commercial exploitation: If marketing a product, process or service, the exploitation plan must include a strategy for that use.
- Conditional — Satellite services: Use Copernicus for Earth observation and/or Galileo or the European Geostationary Navigation Overlay Service for satellite positioning, navigation or timing when using satellite-based Earth observation, positioning, navigation or timing.
- Expected: Report results to the European Partnership on Batteries (the European industry and research initiative) partnership for monitoring of its performance indicators.
- Exception — Results transfers: The granting authority may object to transfers or exclusive licences (giving another party sole rights to use the results) of results for up to four years after project end.
